issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks students to implement config_system that accepts a pointer to a Config struct (problem_statement.md lines 21-22). The solution implementation of config_system (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 6-10) instead treats the argument on the stack as an integer value (mov eax, [esp+4]; add eax, 10) rather than a pointer to a struct. This is a signature/parameter-semantic mismatch: students following the spec will implement pointer-based logic, but the provided solution uses an integer parameter. This discrepancy can confuse students about the expected parameter type and how to access configuration data, and it may lead to incorrect reference solutions or grading expectations.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (A) update the solution implementation so config_system accepts and uses a pointer to a Config struct (e.g., treat [esp+4] as an address and load fields from the pointed struct), or (B) change the problem statement to specify that config_system receives an integer parameter and document its meaning. Prefer option (A) to match the current problem description: modify the solution to dereference the pointer argument and operate on Config fields, and (if helpful) add a stub for config_system in the template so students clearly see the expected signature.
